newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-NOVOTNA MAKES HEAVY WEATHER OF QUARTER-FINAL VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-NOVOTNA MAKES HEAVY WEATHER OF QUARTER-FINAL VICTORY.

text.p: Jana Novotna made hard work of finishing off unseeded Ai Sugiyama to win a place in the semifinals of the rain-hit Eastbourne women's grasscourt tournament on Saturday.
Novotna was just three points away from victory when rain halted play on Friday, at 6-2 6-5 and 15-15 against the Japanese.

But the second-seeded Czech, troubled by the strong winds which buffeted Devonshire Park on Saturday, found it hard to finish off the match. She needed 46 minutes more and three matchpoints before winning through 6-2 6-7 6-4.
In the semifinals later on Saturday, Novotna will meet unseeded Natasha Zvereva of Belarus who despatched Nathalie Tauziat of France 6-4 5-7 6-4 in another quarter-final completed early on Saturday.

Rain played havoc with the schedule on Thursday and Friday and organisers of the $450,000 tournament were hoping to complete two more quarter-finals, the semifinals and the final on Saturday as well as the doubles programme.

Defending champion Monica Seles was back on court against Brenda Schultz-McCarthy of the Netherlands, trailing by one set in a quarter-final delayed from Thursday. Fourth seed Arantxa Sanchez Vicario was playing Romanian Irina Spirlea in the other quarter-final.
Warm winds blew away the rainclouds which have lingered over this seaside resort for two days but brought problems of their own.
Novotna struggled to serve in the wind and allowed Sugiyama back into the game by hitting a double fault to concede the break which took the second set to a tiebreak.
The Czech has carried the stigma of a choker since throwing away the lead to lose the 1993 Wimbledon final to Steffi Graf and her performance on Saturday did little to salvage her reputation.
She hit another double fault at matchpoint in the tiebreak, which Sugiyama went on to win 8-6, and yet another to give the Japanese woman a break early in the deciding set.
But after two breaks apiece Novotna cashed in on a run of mistakes by Sugiyama to wrap up the match after exactly two hours' play.
